songs.title: The Greatest Man Alive
songs.verdict: A Blah Records lifer brags his way through 14 Lee Scott beats, with Jehst, Crimeapple and Black Josh in the guest seats.
songs.body:
King Grubb is a Lancashire emcee and producer from the Blah Records world. He was in Children of the Damned and now raps with its successor, Cult of the Damned. He first went solo in summer 2007 with the Mega Dumb Cheap Shit EP, released as Flash 4dem and fully produced by Blah founder Lee Scott. His first album, Droopy., came out in 2018 with Nobodies Home producing.

The Greatest Man Alive dropped Nov 20, 2026: 14 tracks, all produced by Lee Scott and mixed by Sumgii, with a 12-inch vinyl on Blah. Guests include Crimeapple and Sonnyjim, Black Josh, Sleazy F Baby and Jubbz, Jehst, and Scott himself. The label sells it on outrageous boasts and surreal one-liners about everything from food to moon rocks.

Two reviewers call it jazzy boom bap, with piano, horns and vibraphone, and both think it could outlast Droopy.
songs.scout_note: UK underground (Blah Records, indie label). Listener count not checked, but it should be well under 100k. Sources: legendswillneverdie.com/2026/11/20/king-grubb-the-greatest-man-alive-review/ (Lancashire, CotD/Cult of the Damned, the 2007 Flash 4dem EP produced by Lee Scott, Droopy./Nobodies Home, features, sound, 4/5); undergroundhiphopblog.com/albums/king-grubbs-sophomore-effort-the-greatest-man-alive-prod-by-lee-scott-could-eventually-surpass-droopy-album-review/ (same facts, 8/10); blahrecords.com/products/king-grubb-the-greatest-man-alive-limited-edition-12-vinyl (Lee Scott producing, Sumgii mixing and mastering, tracklist, description of the boasts and the food-to-moon-rocks subjects). Release date Nov 20, 2026 and the 2018 Droopy date come from the Apple Music artist page. Links: I fetched the Apple album URL from the Apple artist page listing. The Bandcamp URL comes from the blahrecords.bandcamp.com label page listing (I removed the ?label= tracking query); the album page itself was blocked, so I didn't open it directly. I left cover_url empty because the only official image was a vinyl mockup on the label store.

songs.title: Another Day in the City
songs.verdict: A CD-out-the-trunk West Coast MC on dusty SP-1200 beats from a producer who found him through a street-corner clip.
songs.body:
Worms Ali is a West Coast underground MC who records, mixes and markets his own music. His bio, per EARMILK, says he sells CDs out of the trunk of his car to pay the bills and fund the next project. In 2024 he put out jazz-leaning boom-bap singles like 'Sup' (prod. Illinformed) and 'That's How It Is' with The Lab Catz.

Producer Retrogott says he found Ali around 2020 through a clip of him selling rap CDs on a street corner, then sent him SP-1200 beats over social media. Their first track was 'Wesside Hashtag', and with no label, manager or plan it grew into an album. The title track came out Nov 11, 2026 with a video. It is the second single from the nine-track Another Day in the City, out Nov 20 on Ill Adrenaline Records.

The pitch is dusty SP-1200 drums, jazz samples and laid-back snapshots of everyday life.
songs.scout_note: Very DIY: a hand-to-hand CD seller on the indie label Ill Adrenaline. Listener count not checked but likely small. Sources: theundergroundhiphop.com/worms-ali-retrogott-another-day-in-the-city-single-and-video-out-now/ (Nov 11 single and video, second single, album out Nov 20 on LP/CD/digital via Ill Adrenaline, the origin story, SP-1200); fatbeats.com/products/worms-ali-retrogott-another-day-in-the-city-cd (9-track list, label IAR065, ships Nov 20, the sound, the 'everyday life' framing); earmilk.com/2024/03/08/worms-ali-share-two-singles-sup-and-thats-how-it-is-featuring-the-lab-catz-video (the CD-trunk bio, self-recorded and self-marketed, the 2024 singles, the Spotify artist link and the Instagram handle). Links: the YouTube URL is the watch form of the embed (youtube.com/embed/ZG42pFdXxjk) on the TUHH post; I didn't fetch it directly. The Spotify artist URL comes from EARMILK. I couldn't verify a Spotify or Apple link for the single itself; the label's ffm.to smart link (foundation-media.ffm.to/aditcsingle) was blocked. Retrogott's hometown isn't sourced, so it's left out.

songs.title: Stray Dogs
songs.verdict: A Salt Lake City lyricist and a Toronto beatmaker turn a cross-border collab into an hour of haunted soul loops and dense, horror-tinged bars.
songs.body:
uMaNg, born Umang Khosla, grew up in Richland, Washington, lived on the East Coast and in Birmingham, England, and now lives in Salt Lake City. He is a boom-bap lifer with tapes like Lasting Impressions II (2023), Not For The Faint of Art (2025, prod. Melvin Junko) and Monu-mEnTaL (2025, prod. B.B.Z Darney). Ben Hedibi is a Toronto producer behind The Ben Gogh Tape (2024) and The Next Level (2025).

Stray Dogs came out Oct 29, 2026 on Dorimania Records. It is their first full-length together, made across state lines and borders, with Hedibi producing and 'Help Less' as a single. The Underground Hip Hop hears haunting soul loops next to high-energy bangers. uMaNg's dense multisyllabic bars and horror-thriller imagery dig into childhood trauma, abandonment and isolation. Most of it was recorded on the spot.

It sits in the lyric-heavy indie boom-bap lane.
songs.scout_note: Tiny: musicmetricsvault showed uMaNg at about 978 monthly Spotify listeners (data around 10 months old). Sources: theundergroundhiphop.com/ben-hedibi-umang-stray-dogs-album/ (Toronto/SLC, debut collab full-length, the sound, the themes, recorded spontaneously, Instagram handles @umangismental and @ben.hedibi); musicmetricsvault.com/artists/umang/3HiQy9etKMyPeuSncy5kNT (birth name, Richland WA, East Coast and Birmingham, earlier tapes and producers); the Apple Music Ben Hedibi artist page (Oct 29, 2026 date, Help Less single, The Ben Gogh Tape 2024, The Next Level 2025). Apple album page: credited 'Umang & Ben Hedibi', label line '℗ 2026 Dorimania Records', 19 songs and 58 minutes. TUHH says 18 tracks, so the critic should check. Links: I fetched the Apple album page directly. The Bandcamp URL comes from the album link on the TUHH post. The cover is the og image on the Apple album page.

songs.title: Don't Feed The Animals (feat. Big Dese)
songs.verdict: A Massachusetts grinder and Boston's Big Dese trade bars over piano stabs and hard drums, with an AI-animated video from a local graphic artist.
songs.body:
Abyss is a Massachusetts rapper working the gritty boom-bap end of the New England underground. Earlier in 2026 he dropped 'Dynamic Duo', produced by DC The Midi Alien. Fellow Massachusetts MC Cyrus Da Zine took a verse and hand-drew the artwork, and Boston turntablist DJ Slipwax closed it out with cuts. Abyss also self-produced 'The Shining', which brought in Queensbridge veteran Tragedy Khadafi, again with Slipwax on the scratches.

'Don't Feed The Animals' arrived Nov 18, 2026, produced by HustleMan Beats. It reunites him with Boston's Big Dese, a rapper known for clever wordplay and viral verses. The Underground Hip Hop calls it dark and gritty, built on piano stabs and hard drums. The video is AI-animated by Boston graphic artist Brian Life, who also made the 'Dynamic Duo' visualizers.

It's a regional underground boom-bap cut, plain and simple.
songs.scout_note: Regional Massachusetts underground; no label mentioned anywhere. Listener count not checked, but probably small. Sources: theundergroundhiphop.com/abyss-connects-with-big-dese-for-dont-feed-the-animals-prod-by-hustleman-beats/ (Nov 18 post, HustleMan Beats, Big Dese described as Boston's own with wordplay and viral verses, the 'once again' team-up, piano stabs and drums, AI video by Brian Life); thehypemagazine.com/2026/05/25/abyss-ft-cyrus-da-zine-dynamic-duo/ ('Dynamic Duo', DC The Midi Alien, Cyrus Da Zine's verse and artwork, DJ Slipwax, Brian Life visualizers); rockthebells.com/articles/abyss-drops-the-shining-featuring-tragedy-khadafi (self-produced 'The Shining' with Tragedy Khadafi and DJ Slipwax; the article is undated). Links: the YouTube URL is the watch form of the embed (youtube.com/embed/OwFxvof2fJA) on the TUHH post; I didn't fetch it directly. The song.link page (song.link/dont-feed-the-animals) was blocked, so there is no Spotify or Apple link. I found an Audiomack page (audiomack.com/abyssthemc) and a Bandcamp page (abysshiphop.bandcamp.com) but couldn't confirm they belong to the same Abyss, so I left them out. Check that this is the right Abyss before publishing.

songs.title: YES
songs.verdict: A Cape Town trio's debut that, by every press account, drags post-punk grit through hyperpop distortion and alt-rap, with Kenny Mason and Ledbyher along for the ride.
songs.body:
Internet Girl are a Cape Town trio formed in 2019: vocalist TK (Ntsika) plus Neese and Griggs on production. They have played Boiler Room Soweto and Pitchfork Music Festival Paris, co-headlined South Africa's Kiss Kiss Festival with Basement Jaxx, and landed "PULL UP" on the NBA 2K27 soundtrack.

YES is their debut album, out 13 November 2026 on PACK. Records: ten tracks written, performed and produced by the band, mostly on a week-long Karoo trip in early 2026. Kenny Mason turns up on "DA BUSINESS" (met via DMs) with Ledbyher on "BIG SAN TONY". The title is an ad-lib TK kept repeating, and the band tie it to acting on instinct; the songs circle coming of age and self-assurance.

Press puts them between post-punk, hyperpop and alt hip-hop. Grimy Goods heard the October single "HIGH AS HEAVEN" as alarm-like synths and filtered screamo vocals tipping into chaotic rapping.
songs.scout_note: Why: hyperpop/alt-rap crossover debut LP, released inside the window (13 Nov 2026), indie label (PACK. Records; Apple/Shazam label line reads 'Create / Pack Records - JV'), no major deal. Doubt: listener count unknown and they have NBA 2K27 + Pitchfork Paris + Boiler Room credits, so CHECK SPOTIFY MONTHLY LISTENERS; they may sit above 100k. Sources: formation 2019, members TK/Neese/Griggs, PACK., Boiler Room Soweto, Pitchfork Paris, Kiss Kiss Festival w/ Basement Jaxx, NBA 2K27 'PULL UP', Karoo writing trip, Kenny Mason via DMs, title from TK ad-lib, themes: Dork 23 Sep 2026 https://readdork.com/news/internet-girl-yes-da-business-kenny-mason-bb5816e3bd ; release date, 10 tracks, written/performed/produced by Internet Girl, features, Cape Town, cover: Bandcamp https://internetgirl.bandcamp.com/album/yes ; post-punk/hyperpop/alt hip-hop tag, HIGH AS HEAVEN out 21 Oct, tour from NYC 11 Nov: PLAYY. https://theplayground.co.uk/internet-girl-map-out-debut-album-rollout-for-yes/ ; HIGH AS HEAVEN description (alarm synth, filtered screamo vocals, chaotic rapping): Grimy Goods 26 Oct 2026 https://www.grimygoods.com/2026/10/26/3-new-songs-to-hear-from-mareux-she-wants-revenge-and-internet-girl/ (also in their Oct 2026 best-songs list). Note: ArtistRack (paid promo) lists griggs as guitarist, Dork says Neese and Griggs are producers; body hedges. Links: bandcamp_url fetched directly (album page, date and tracklist confirmed). apple_url taken from Shazam album page https://www.shazam.com/album/6795678238/yes, whose track links all point to music.apple.com/us/album/.../6795678238; I removed the ?i= track and tracking parameters to leave the album page, so click once to confirm. No Spotify album link found. Single video for HIGH AS HEAVEN exists (YouTube embed W_BHzFaxYBc on Grimy Goods) but it is a single, not the album, so left out of youtube_url. artist_ig not found on an official source. Lane note from this scout: hyperpop lane research was badly limited (web search budget ran out, many fetches blocked), so this is the only fully sourced pick; unverified leads: FLVCKKA 'Hypercorridos Vol.1' (Ones To Watch 9 Oct 2026, release date unconfirmed), Katherine Aly '222.2' EP (22 Oct 2026, The Skinny, facts thin), vincethealien 'ELONGATED TIME' (EARMILK 28 Oct 2026, facts thin), Kennydubone 's0n' (Muzic.NZ 12 Oct 2026, facts thin).

songs.title: Little Green Book
songs.verdict: Auckland guitar band trading Flying Nun jangle for something louder and rawer, with discordant verses that blow open into a distorted, shouted chorus about grief.
songs.body:
Awning are a five-piece from Auckland, New Zealand, led by singer Christian Dimick. The band began as Dimick recording lo-fi, folky demos alone in a shed. It became a live five-piece around 2023, with Riley Noonan, Damin McCabe, Ethan Broughton and Eli Chamberlain. A self-titled EP followed in 2025, and earlier this year they supported Wednesday on their New Zealand tour.

"Little Green Book" came out on October 6, 2026, as their first single for LA indie label Winspear, home of Slow Pulp and Wishy. De Sevens produced it at Neil Finn's Roundhead Studios, and McCabe directed the video. Dimick says it's about grief, with deliberately cryptic lyrics that keep some privacy.

Clash sets them between Flying Nun minimalism and Husker Du. The debut album is due January 29, with SXSW and The Great Escape after that.
songs.scout_note: Stereogum 'Band To Watch' feature (Nov 17, 2026) plus signing/single coverage on Stereogum, The Line of Best Fit and Clash (all Oct 6, 2026); Dork also covered the album announcement. Lane: guitar indie rock / NZ. Winspear is an indie label; no listener count found, so check it, but this is a fresh signing with an EP behind them. Sources: https://stereogum.com/2513715/awning-little-green-book/music (release date, Winspear second international signing, grief quote paraphrase, McCabe video); https://www.thelineofbestfit.com/news/new-zealand-band-awning-sign-to-winspear-and-release-new-song-little-green-book (members, self-titled EP last year, label mates Slow Pulp/Wishy/Swapmeet); https://www.clashmusic.com/?p=463150 (Roundhead Studios, producer De Sevens, Wednesday NZ tour support, Flying Nun/Husker Du comparison); https://stereogum.com/2517682/band-to-watch-awning/interviews/band-to-watch (shed demos origin, five-piece since ~2023, album date 1/29, SXSW/Great Escape). Doubt: Stereogum calls the 2025 release a self-titled album, LOBF calls it an EP. I used EP. Link check: the YouTube ID comes from the video embed in both the Stereogum and Clash single posts. I converted youtube.com/embed/qbdOlFfVa_8 to a watch URL. I could not fetch YouTube directly, so confirm it plays. No Spotify, Apple or Bandcamp link was found, so those are left blank.

songs.title: The Big Picture
songs.verdict: Minneapolis trio's first song for Closed Casket, written up as darker and heavier than their debut, with a wall of fuzz and a moshable breakdown in the Hum and Jawbox lineage.
songs.body:
Prize Horse are a Minneapolis trio: Jake Beitel on guitar and vocals, Olivia Johnson on bass and Jon Brenner on drums. They debuted in 2021 and put out the Welder EP in 2022. Their 2024 debut album Under Sound, produced by Gleemer's Corey Coffman, came out on Chicago's New Morality Zine. Stereogum listed it among its favorite albums of 2024 and named them a favorite new act.

"The Big Picture" arrived October 19, 2026, as their first single for Closed Casket Activities, the hardcore label from Troy, New York. It's the first song written for a still-unannounced record, with demos going back to 2023. The band say it's darker and more brooding than Under Sound and ends on one of the heaviest sections they've written. Lyrically, it's about days when nothing feels right and every choice feels like too much.

Stereogum hears Hum and Jawbox in it.
songs.scout_note: Covered by Stereogum (Tom Breihan) and The Line of Best Fit on Oct 19, 2026. Lane: heavy shoegaze / emo-grunge. Closed Casket is an indie label. No listener count found. They may sit near the upper edge of 'underground' after the 2024 Stereogum praise, so check the number. Sources: https://stereogum.com/2514991/prize-horse-the-big-picture/music (date, Closed Casket move, demos from 2023, darker/heavier quote paraphrase, lyrics theme, Hum/Jawbox comparison, Under Sound on Stereogum year-end lists); https://www.thelineofbestfit.com/news/minneapolis-trio-prize-horse-sign-to-closed-casket-activities-and-share-new-single (2021 debut, Welder EP 2022, Troy NY label, shared stages, December dates with Spite House); https://thecurrent.org/feature/2024/04/10/minnesota-music-month-scouting-report-2024-prize-horse (member names, Corey Coffman producer, New Morality Zine Chicago). Link check: the YouTube ID comes from the embed in the Stereogum single post, converted from embed to watch format. Not fetched directly, so confirm it plays. An Apple search hit (song/1888216993) turned out to be a different artist and was NOT used.

songs.title: seed
songs.verdict: St. Louis DIY lifers on a scraggly, discordant single of whirling guitars and pounding drums that slows down in its back half, recorded mostly live at a house venue.
songs.body:
Shady Bug have been part of the Midwestern DIY scene in St. Louis for nearly a decade, with Hannah Rainey on vocals. Their first album, tbh idk (2017), was recorded at the Nest, a house venue. Lemon Lime followed in 2019 and the What's The Use? EP in 2023.

"seed" came out October 1, 2026, as the second single from I wanted to be there, released October 30 by Julia's War Recordings with Bee Side Cassettes. Julia's War is the Philadelphia label run by Doug Dulgarian of They Are Gutting A Body Of Water. The band cut the 14-track album in a 10-day session with Scoops Dardaris, mostly live at the Nest. The song is about how someone who's only briefly in your life can affect it far more than you expected.

It follows the fuzz-pop lead single "my night routine" and fits the Julia's War orbit of scrappy, loud-quiet indie rock.
songs.scout_note: Two Stereogum posts (album announcement Sep 3, 2026; 'seed' Oct 1, 2026). Lane: DIY indie rock / fuzz pop. Julia's War is a small indie label. Listener count unknown but very likely small. Sources: https://stereogum.com/2510261/shady-bug-announce-new-album-i-wanted-to-be-there-hear-my-night-routine/music (nearly a decade in Midwestern DIY, tbh idk 2017 at the Nest, Lemon Lime 2019, What's The Use? EP 2023, Bernie comp, Julia's War/Dulgarian, Scoops Dardaris 10-day session, 14 tracks, Oct 30 date); https://stereogum.com/2513188/shady-bug-seed/music (Oct 1 release, Hannah Rainey vocals, song theme paraphrase, sound description). The 'Julia's War orbit' line in the body is my lane framing, not a press quote. Link check: the YouTube ID comes from the 'seed' video embed on Stereogum, converted to watch format and not fetched directly. The Bandcamp URL is the album page (which includes 'seed') linked from both Stereogum posts. My own fetch of Bandcamp was blocked, so confirm the release is live.

songs.title: The Scene Is Changing
songs.verdict: Nashville trio's Saddle Creek debut, produced by feeble little horse's Sebastian Kinsler and compared in press to early Soccer Mommy: fuzzy '90s-pop choruses aimed at the life cycle of a DIY scene.
songs.body:
Baby Wave are a Nashville trio of multi-instrumentalists: book NOT brooke, Gardner Gottsegen and Jakob Bibb. They came together at a 2021 Christmas party and mix slowcore, slacker rock, emo and shoegaze. Before this they released the You Me &, EP in 2023 and still life, a 2024 joint EP with Total Wife. They've played with Hotline TNT, feeble little horse, Annie DiRusso and Snõõper.

"The Scene Is Changing" came out October 6, 2026, as their first song for Saddle Creek, with a debut album on the way. Sebastian Kinsler of feeble little horse produced it. book NOT brooke says it began as a character study and turned into a song for Nashville's ever-changing DIY scene, about how scenes bloom, peak and fade. The video was shot at the house venue Ryman 2.

Stereogum compares the choruses to early Soccer Mommy.
songs.scout_note: Signing and single covered by Stereogum, The Line of Best Fit and BroadwayWorld (all Oct 6, 2026). They're on The Line of Best Fit's discovery playlists. Lane: Nashville DIY slowcore / shoegaze. Saddle Creek is an established indie label, not a major. Listener count unknown, likely small, but check. Sources: https://stereogum.com/2513735/baby-wave-the-scene-is-changing/music (2021 Christmas party, Kinsler producer, Soccer Mommy comparison, Ryman 2 video and cameo bands, Swapmeet tour); https://www.thelineofbestfit.com/news/baby-wave-sign-to-saddle-creek-and-share-new-song-the-scene-is-changing (members, You Me &, EP 2023, still life 2024, song-meaning paraphrase, past collaborators); https://www.broadwayworld.com/article/Baby-Wave-Sign-to-Saddle-Creek-with-New-Single-This-Fall-20261006 (genre blend, debut album to be announced, Instagram handle from the press release). Link check: the same YouTube ID (XlnECE9od0k) is embedded in both the Stereogum and BroadwayWorld posts, converted to watch format and not fetched directly.

songs.title: Fast Strong Horse
songs.verdict: Experimental noise-rock duo's self-described 'pop song,' which press describe as moving from electric drones and somber vocals into a percussion-heavy stretch with brass.
songs.body:
Or Best Offer are Grace Schmidhauser (vocals, guitar) and Brian Culligan (drums, synths). Oh My Rockness described them as spanning Chicago, Brooklyn and Providence and called their sound experimental ambient noise rock. It recommended them to fans of Gastr Del Sol, Godspeed You! Black Emperor and Fennesz. Their album Center came out on Ba Da Bing Records.

"Fast Strong Horse" came out October 30, 2026, when they joined Good English Records, a newish NY/Nashville label whose roster includes Crate and Billboard Style. It leads It Will Appear, a nine-track album due January 15, 2027. The title comes from the last lines of Clarice Lispector's first novel, Near to the Wild Heart. Schmidhauser calls it the record's pop song, written during a rough stretch to get back some sanity and dignity.

It sits in the slow-build experimental rock lane, closer to post-rock than bedroom pop.
songs.scout_note: Stereogum album announcement (Margaret Farrell, Oct 30, 2026). Lane: experimental / ambient noise rock. Both labels are small indies (Good English; earlier Ba Da Bing). Listener count unknown but very likely small. Sources: https://stereogum.com/2516091/or-best-offer-announce-new-album-it-will-appear-hear-fast-strong-horse/music (members, Good English and roster, It Will Appear Jan 15 2027 with nine tracks, Lispector title source, 'pop song' paraphrase, sound description, Ella Sinskey video); https://www.ohmyrockness.com/bands/or-best-offer (Chicago/Brooklyn/Providence, instruments, 'experimental ambient noise rock', RIYL list, Center on Ba Da Bing; profile dated Jan 2024). Doubt: Stereogum calls them a New York duo, Oh My Rockness says they span three cities. Link check: the YouTube ID comes from the video embed in the Stereogum post, converted to watch format and not fetched directly. artist_url is the Bandcamp root linked from Oh My Rockness. My fetch of it was blocked, so confirm it.

songs.title: What I Meant To Say
songs.verdict: A jazz-schooled multi-instrumentalist who writes, plays, produces and mixes nearly everything himself bends his alt-R&B toward detuned, electro-acoustic pop on his second album.
songs.body:
Quinn Oulton is a London multi-instrumentalist, singer and producer (Clash placed him in Brighton in September) who came up out of classical jazz. His 2022 debut album Alexithymia leaned jazz-adjacent, and along the way he has teamed up with Moses Boyd on 'Clashing Colours' and with Col3trane on 'Lately'.

What I Meant To Say, his second album, came out on 13 November 2026 via Frequency. It runs 13 tracks, and he produced, wrote, performed and mixed all of it except a cover of Pixies' 'Where Is My Mind?'. Singles 'Comfort Food', 'Catastrophe' and 'Can We Stay Here Please' set it up. That last one was written as he was leaving Lagrasse, a medieval village in southern France, dreading the return to city life and the online grind.

Press files it under alt-R&B, progressive soul and experimental pop. A UK and European tour follows in February 2027, with stops at The Lexington and Paradiso.
songs.scout_note: Alt-R&B lane. Released 13 Nov 2026 on Frequency. Listeners: Music Metrics Vault shows about 64.2k monthly and 14.8k followers (marked 'updated 2 months ago'), so under the bar; there is no sign of a major label. Sources: Clash 13 Nov 2026 (https://www.clashmusic.com/news/quinn-oulton-unveils-new-album-what-i-meant-to-say) for the label, the second-album status, the singles, the genre framing and the tour. Clash 14 Sep 2026 (https://www.clashmusic.com/news/quinn-oulton-announces-new-album-what-i-meant-to-say/) for Brighton-based, the 2022 Alexithymia debut, Catastrophe, and the Lagrasse story. Dork 13 Nov 2026 (https://readdork.com/news/quinn-oulton-released-second-album-what-i) for the London base, the release date and the Moses Boyd 'Clashing Colours' single. Bandcamp album page for the tracklist and credits (self-produced except the Pixies cover). Bandcamp artist page lists the Col3trane track 'Lately'. Stereofox (https://www.stereofox.com/quinn-oulton-can-we-stay-here-please/) is a backup source for Lagrasse. Doubt: Clash said Brighton in September, while Dork, the November Clash piece and Bandcamp say London. Links: the Spotify album URL is copied from Dork's 'Listen on Spotify' link and matches the album ID in Clash's embed. The Bandcamp album page was fetched (13 Nov 2026, 13 tracks). The cover comes from that page. The IG handle and Spotify artist URL come from the links on his official Bandcamp page. There is a YouTube video embedded in Clash/Dork (CJGfp73A4lk), but neither page says which song it is, so I left it out.

songs.title: ADSM (Afro Diasporic Soul Music)
songs.verdict: Lagos-born, Ireland-raised and London-based, Caleb Kunle folds gospel, soul and Yoruba heritage into a five-track debut EP built around a love song called 'Heartline'.
songs.body:
Caleb Kunle was born in Lagos, grew up in Ireland and lives in London. He describes his framework, The Black Future Now, as a meeting of ancestral Yoruba tradition and futurist sound. He has played the Barbican and the Royal Festival Hall, supported Fatoumata Diawara and Lianne La Havas, made the Glastonbury Emerging Talent finals and was shortlisted for MOBO Unsung 2025.

ADSM (Afro Diasporic Soul Music) is his five-track debut EP, released in mid-November 2026 on Stereofox Records. Alex Wildwood, Lucas Polo and Aidan Glover produced it, Danny Trachtenberg mixed it, and the PRS Foundation's Open Fund helped pay to finish it. 'Something Better' and the centrepiece 'Heartline' came out ahead of it. The EP deals with identity, self-worth, grief and joy, with a Black History Month nod to his Nigerian roots.

It mixes soul, gospel, R&B and hip-hop. A debut album, Joyful Noise, is planned.
songs.scout_note: Underground-soul lane. Debut EP on the indie label Stereofox Records. I couldn't find a listener count; it is likely small, but please check. Release date: Stereofox (26 Oct 2026) says 16 Nov, and Acid Stag wrote it up on 19 Nov 2026. Sources: Acid Stag (https://acidstag.com/2026/11/caleb-kunle-adsm-ep/) for Lagos, Ireland and London, the Stereofox Records debut, five tracks, and the genres and themes. PRS Foundation (https://prsfoundation.com/grantees/caleb-kunle-the-open-fund/) for The Black Future Now, the producers, the mixer, the Open Fund, the Barbican and RFH shows, the Diawara and La Havas support slots, Glastonbury Emerging Talent, MOBO Unsung 2025 and the Joyful Noise album plan. Note that PRS had expected a late-summer 2026 release, so it slipped. Stereofox (https://www.stereofox.com/caleb-kunle-heartline/) calls Heartline the centrepiece and second single and mentions the Black History Month and Nigerian-roots angle. Hot Press 2 Oct 2026 (https://www.hotpress.com/music/new-irish-songs-to-hear-this-week-278-23163488) covers 'Something Better' as the first single. Note that Stereofox is both his label and one of the outlets covering him. Links: the Spotify album URL is converted from the album embed (5Bs4TetlDnKGQekReP4AWL) in Acid Stag's ADSM EP post. I didn't open Spotify directly, so confirm it resolves to ADSM. The 'Heartline' single is https://open.spotify.com/track/4rjivRRKVjvfZOyx9cY6jo (from Stereofox) if you want the single instead. I found no official IG handle.

songs.title: Ugly Face
songs.verdict: Sacramento-born brothers who spent years writing for Chris Brown and others slow things down on a late-night bedroom cut from their new EP.
songs.body:
Blaq Tuxedo are the brothers Darius and Dom Logan. They were born in Sacramento, wrote songs together as kids and moved to Los Angeles in 2009 to write professionally. They started out as D&D with a 2012 project, Unforgettable, then renamed themselves. Their writing credits include 'Anyway', 'Little Bit' and 'Who's Gonna' on Chris Brown's Royalty. They have released the Limousine EP, the Red Flowerz EP (with Bibi Bourelly, IAMSU! and Ty Dolla $ign), the Tap In mixtape with DJ Carisma, and the 2017 album ABA (Art By Accident), which featured E-40 on 'Lit'.

'Ugly Face' landed in early November 2026. Rated R&B describes it as a slower bedroom song that follows 'Crash Out' and 'No Curfew'. All three are on their EP Boyz in the Band, set for 13 November.

Rated R&B calls them an alt-R&B duo: songwriters' songwriters stepping back into the spotlight.
songs.scout_note: Alt-R&B lane. These are veteran songwriters rather than a brand-new act. Check the listener count and whether they have a label; I found neither. Rated R&B listed the single in its 7 Nov 2026 roundup (https://ratedrnb.com/2026/11/9-essential-new-rb-releases-ella-mai-chloe-charlie-wilson-more/), which is the source for the alt-R&B duo label, the bedroom framing, the earlier singles 'Crash Out' and 'No Curfew', and the EP Boyz in the Band due Nov 13. The background comes from a 2017 Audible Treats press release (https://audibletreats.com/?p=37703): Darius and Dom Logan, Sacramento, the 2009 LA move, D&D and Unforgettable (2012), the Chris Brown Royalty credits, Tap In, Red Flowerz, Limousine, ABA, and 'Lit' with E-40. The same release also claims a 2014 Grammy nomination, which I left out of the body as unverified. The 2015 date for Limousine comes from the Rated R&B URL (ratedrnb.com/2015/09/listen-blaq-tuxedos-limousine-ep/), which I did not fetch. The exact single date is not confirmed; it was out by 7 Nov. Link: the Spotify URL is converted from the track embed in the Rated R&B post. Weakest pick in my lane; swap it if something better turns up.

songs.title: Drive By Strokes / Primrose Mountain
songs.verdict: A Bedford producer makes his Hessle Audio debut with two quick, stripped-back UK club tracks; Ben UFO, Call Super and Surusinghe were playing them before release.
songs.body:
Sam Girling is a producer and DJ born and based in Bedford. Alongside his own records he runs the party series and label Attacca. 2026 has been busy for him: 'Look What U Done' in February, a remix of The Avalanches' 'Since I Left You' in May, and a vinyl-only 'oh bby / gott wood?' in July that has since sold out.

Drive By Strokes / Primrose Mountain (HES054) came out on 3 November 2026 as his debut on Hessle Audio. It is a two-tracker with extended mixes, and he wrote, produced and mixed it himself. Matt Colton mastered and cut it at Metropolis, and the 12-inch is due in January 2027. The label calls it a euphoric but stripped-back turn toward late-night UK club music. Boomkat calls it big-room-ready, speedy UKG. Girling singles out Ben UFO closing Dekmantel with 'Drive By Strokes' as a highlight.

The label itself links the record to Hessle's genre-blurring early-2010s releases.
songs.scout_note: Left-field electronic (UKG/club). Out 3 Nov 2026 on Hessle Audio, an indie label. Chartmetric shows about 78.6k Spotify monthly listeners and 6.3k followers (refreshed 19 Nov 2026, https://chartmetric.com/artist/783896), so he is under the bar but close; recheck. RA covered it in 'This week's new music' on 6 Nov 2026 (https://ra.co/news/86334). Sources: the Bandcamp release page for the date, the Bedford base, Attacca, the self-credits, Matt Colton at Metropolis, the earlier 2026 releases, and the Ben UFO/Call Super/Surusinghe support. Boomkat (https://boomkat.com/artists/sam-girling/releases/axxp2g7i/drive-by-strokes-primrose-mountain) for HES054 and its blurb. Cold Cuts Hot Wax (https://coldcutshotwax.uk/products/sam-girling-drive-by-strokes-primrose-mountain) for the vinyl date (15 Jan 2027), the Dekmantel quote and the early-2010s Hessle reference. Links: the Spotify track page was fetched (Drive By Strokes, Sam Girling, 3 Nov 2026). The Tidal album page was fetched and matches the title and date. The Bandcamp page was fetched. The cover image and the IG and RA links come from his official Bandcamp page. A Hessle Audio SoundCloud upload showed up in search, but SoundCloud blocks fetching, so I left it out.

songs.title: Chosen One EP
songs.verdict: Copenhagen's UK-garage lifer arrives on Nervous Horizon with three tracks that run from soulful garage-house to a dubby 4x4 roller and a grime-MC amapiano hybrid.
songs.body:
Main Phase is Adam Schierbeck, a Copenhagen producer who started collecting garage vinyl at 14. He was in the Henri's Garage crew that threw a UK garage night in the city in 2014, and he later ran the Pure Butter parties at Baggen. His first EPs came out on Warehouse Raves, with further records on ec2a and Hardline Sounds. He co-founded ATW Records with his close collaborator Interplanetary Criminal during lockdown.

Chosen One came out on 23 October 2026, his first release for Nervous Horizon. 'Creep Into My Mind' is soulful, garage-leaning house. The title track adds dubby bass and Jamaican-style vocals over a 4x4 beat. 'Take Time' brings in Willesden grime MC Logan and mixes jungle, UK funky and amapiano. The label pitches it as a bridge from his older work to a newer sound.

It sits in the bass-heavy garage scene he has spent a decade trying to grow in Copenhagen.
songs.scout_note: Left-field electronic (UKG/bass). Indie label Nervous Horizon. Doubt: he is well established in UK bass circles (ATW with Interplanetary Criminal, an RA podcast, a Rinse show), and I could not get a listener count. He may be over 100k, so check before keeping, and swap him if he is. Sources: the Bandcamp release page for the 23 Oct 2026 date, the tracklist with Logan, the description and the 'bridge' framing. Dance Wax 29 Oct 2026 (https://dancewax.net/2026/10/29/main-phase-joins-nervous-horizons-with-chosen-one-ep/) for the Nervous Horizon debut, the track descriptions and Logan as a Willesden grime MC. Groove 23 Oct 2026 (https://groove.de/2026/10/23/die-platten-der-woche-mit-dj-godfather-main-phase-musuama-nachtbraker-und-nathan-fake/) for the dub bass and Jamaican-style vocals and the jungle/amapiano mix on Take Time. Mixmag 19 Oct 2026 (https://mixmag.net/read/new-music-on-our-radar-this-week-sophia-stel-chris-stassy-nesa-azadikhah-news) also lists it. UKF 2023 (https://ukf.com/read/we-need-to-talk-about-main-phase/) for his real name, garage vinyl at 14, Warehouse Raves, ec2a, Hardline and ATW. DJ Mag (https://djmag.com/features/inside-copenhagens-bass-fuelled-garage-scene) for Henri's Garage in 2014 and Pure Butter at Baggen. Links: the Spotify album URL is converted from the album embed in the Dance Wax EP post; I didn't open it directly. The Bandcamp page was fetched, and the cover comes from it.
